A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Toolathlon benchmark and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. Full-document text comparison and page rendering support a reliable comparison; all appendix pages are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on 108 tasks in Section 4 and Table 3, with additional quantitative analyses and observed execution trajectories in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original evaluations, quantitative analyses, and appendix case studies, including the model success rates in Table 3.

M1.justification: The benchmark framework, agent loop, and tool-error, output-length, and context-management components are unchanged. Section 2.4 adds tool-selection details without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 108 tasks across 32 applications and 604 MCP tools, with unchanged domains and appendix scenarios. Updated descriptions of other benchmarks in Table 1 do not change the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated model configurations in Table 3 and the comparison participants in supplementary analyses are unchanged. Table 1 also retains the same benchmark membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same evaluation metrics, 100-turn limit, and task-specific server selection. v2's explicit server-count and tool-loading details clarify the existing setup rather than revise a previously stated setting.

E4.justification: Section 5 and Appendices C and E retain the same tool-error, trajectory-length, overlong-output, cost, and token analyses, together with the same failure cases and execution trajectories.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three evaluations per model and report mean pass@1 with standard deviation, alongside pass@3 and pass^3. Run-count and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The descriptive comparison in Table 1 revises MCP-RADAR's reported size from 300 tasks and 9 apps to 507 tasks and 6 apps. Toolathlon's experimental results remain unchanged, including Claude-4.5-Sonnet's 38.6% and DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp's 20.1% success rates in Table 3.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 retains the same POMDP formulation, spaces, transition function, and reward definition. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning diverse, realistic, long-horizon evaluation and the same claims about current models' shortcomings. The revised benchmark comparison does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning premature termination, long-context difficulties, tool errors, reasoning effort, and inconsistent task completion are unchanged in Sections 4–5 and the appendices. No substantive limitation or applicability boundary is added.

D1.justification: Section 2.4 now explicitly states that each task exposes fewer than ten necessary MCP servers, rather than all 32, and loads every tool from each selected server without further filtering or retrieval. These are additional implementation disclosures; resource links and appendix implementation details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Table 1 refines prior-work positioning by separating real environments from state initialization and explicitly identifying partial initialization in ACEBench and LiveMCPBench. It also revises benchmark characterizations and MCP-RADAR's counts. The cited works and Section 6 narrative remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: Table 1's caption explains BFCLv3-MT and the revised comparison criteria, its erroneous 'Appendix 6' reference becomes Section 6, and Section 2.4 gains clarification. Section order and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 splits the combined 'Real States & Init' column into 'Real Env' and 'States Init', expands its caption, and changes the fuzzy-prompt heading. Associated layout changes are local; other tables, figures, and appendix pages remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency about which tools agents actually receive and makes Table 1 more informative by separating environment realism from state initialization. These changes reduce ambiguity in the evaluation setup and prior-work comparison. The empirical evidence and central conclusions remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
